instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, changing the water until it runs clear, then drain it. Put the rice in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on until the curry is ready.
Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes. Cut the carrots, green beans and zucchini into sticks about 2 inches long and as thick as a finger.
Put the coconut, cumin seeds and green chilies in a blender with 1/2 cup water. Blend to a smooth, thick paste and set it aside.
Put the potatoes in a wide pot with 2 cups water and 1 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots, green beans, 1 sprig of the curry leaves and the turmeric. Cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the zucchini, cover, and cook for 3 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender but keep their shape.
Stir in the coconut paste and boil on medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the raw coconut smell is gone and the liquid has thickened.
Stir in 1 tsp of the coconut oil. Take the pot off the heat.
Whisk the yogurt until smooth and stir it in. Keep the pot off the heat, or the yogurt will curdle.
Heat the remaining 2 tsp coconut oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds. They will pop after about 30 seconds, so stand back a little.
Add the urad dal, the other sprig of curry leaves and the asafoetida. Stir for 30 seconds, until the dal is golden. Pour it all over the avial and stir.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen (Udupi style, 4.98 from 265) is the lead: potatoes first, the other vegetables in stages, a smooth coconut, cumin and green chili paste, yogurt stirred in off the heat, and a mustard seed and curry leaf tempering. The two other readable versions (Cooking Curries 5 from 6 votes, Raks Kitchen 5 from 2) agree on the method but have too few ratings to lead. The traditional drumstick, yam, raw banana, tindora and long beans are swapped for potato, carrot, green beans and zucchini so it can be shopped at an ordinary store, with the amount raised to make it a main with rice. The lead's dried red chilies are left out to keep the base mild. Desiccated coconut is used in place of fresh, which the lead allows.
